sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species is difficult to identify reliably from soldiers or alates alone: it is morphologically intermediate within the genus and requires the enteric valve armature of workers and soldiers, the soldier mandibular shape and the geographic origin in combination. Soldier medium-sized, head length (to the anterior margin of the clypeus) 2.70—3.45 mm, the enteric valve generally recognizable as the finitimus type; frontal protuberance very small or absent, the upper margin of the head only slightly concave. Compared with I. planifrons, the mandibular curvature changes more rapidly along the length of the mandible (difference of the log curvature of the left mandible 1.28—2.42, versus 0.89—2.28 in the latter), i.e. the mandible is straighter at the base and more strongly curved apically; the soldier mandibles of I. planifrons are on average slightly more strongly curved. Alate medium-sized, head width (across the compound eyes) 1.47—1.71 mm. Worker of medium size within the genus. Ecology and distribution aid identification: the species is always found in continental forest east of 15°E, and its range overlaps that of I. planifrons only in south-western Central African Republic.

note: Adapted from the species-level diagnosis in the revision by Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the measurement abbreviations have been replaced by descriptive Chinese names in line with the definitions of the original table. The original states that a single caste is difficult to identify and that identification rests mainly on the combination of worker enteric valve armature, soldier mandibles and locality; this entry records only the diagnostic characters that can be stated and does not transcribe the item-by-item measurement tables of the morphological descriptions.
